subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw continue supporting Host-header origin fallback as an operator-selected dangerous mode, or should the gateway remove or additionally harden that mode for network-exposed Control UI deployments?
rationale: The exact exploit path is not proven, and repository security policy treats dangerous operator flags as break-glass tradeoffs, but changing or removing the flag affects a documented security-sensitive gateway configuration.

options.title: Keep flag, add targeted hardening
options.body: Preserve the documented dangerous mode for compatibility while adding a maintainer-approved defense such as `Sec-Fetch-Site` checks, clearer audit/docs, or tighter tests if security reviewers confirm the remaining browser risk.

options.title: Remove fallback with migration
options.body: Delete the flag and require explicit `allowedOrigins`, but include upgrade handling and docs because this changes an intentional config surface.

options.title: Accept current model
options.body: Close the security question as an explicit operator-risk tradeoff under `SECURITY.md`, leaving the critical audit and documentation as the supported mitigation.

recommendation.title: Keep flag, add targeted hardening
recommendation.body: Preserve the documented dangerous mode for compatibility while adding a maintainer-approved defense such as `Sec-Fetch-Site` checks, clearer audit/docs, or tighter tests if security reviewers confirm the remaining browser risk.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the closest merged trusted-proxy HTTP origin hardening and has recent history on the affected gateway auth/origin path.
